overview.title: The Magic of a Saharan Bivouac
overview.p1: Overnight under the stars on the edge of the erg. Staying at a desert camp in Merzouga is an unforgettable highlight: experience golden dunes, traditional Berber hospitality, and quiet desert nights.
overview.p2: Most camps offer comfortable private tents equipped with proper beds, lanterns, and options for en-suite bathrooms, blending rustic charm with modern comfort.
overview.p3: Evenings are spent sharing tagines around the campfire, listening to traditional drum rhythms, and admiring the brilliant Milky Way overhead.

food.title: Dining in the Desert
food.p1: Desert dining is a central part of the bivouac experience, featuring hearty traditional meals prepared on-site.
food.li1: Welcome mint tea upon arrival at camp
food.li2: Traditional Moroccan tagine cooked over coals
food.li3: Fresh seasonal fruits and Moroccan sweets
food.li5: Special dietary options available upon advance request
food.p2: All meals are included with your desert camp booking, as there are no external restaurants out in the dunes.

tips.title: Practical Tips for Your Desert Stay

1.title: Pack Warm Layers
1.desc: Desert temperatures drop sharply at night — bring a jacket, fleece or sweater.

2.title: Light Luggage
2.desc: Pack a small overnight backpack for the dunes and leave heavy suitcases at your base hotel in Merzouga.

3.title: Footwear & Protection
3.desc: Bring sunglasses, sunscreen, comfortable walking shoes or sandals for the sand.

q1.question: How long do I need at a Desert Camp?
q1.answer: An overnight stay is standard, usually arriving by camel or 4x4 in the late afternoon and leaving after breakfast.

q2.question: What is included in a desert camp stay?
q2.answer: Most stays include a private or shared tent, dinner, breakfast, camel trek or 4x4 transfer, and evening music around the campfire.

q3.question: Are there private bathrooms in desert camps?
q3.answer: Luxury desert camps feature private en-suite bathrooms with hot showers, while standard camps offer clean shared facilities.

q4.question: Is it cold at night in the desert?
q4.answer: Yes, desert temperatures drop significantly after sunset, especially during autumn, winter, and spring. Warm layers are essential.

q5.question: How do you get to the desert camp?
q5.answer: Guests typically reach the camp via a camel caravan ride across the dunes or via a 4x4 desert transfer arranged by the camp.
